newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S. yacht to rescue reed boat from Easter Island.
newsitem.headline: U.S. yacht to rescue reed boat from Easter Island.

text.p: A reed raft sailing across the Pacific from Chile's Easter Island seemed to have reached the end of its mission after its bow broke in a storm, Chilean naval authorities said on Saturday.
A U.S. yacht in the area, the Stray Dog, is expected to reach the shipwreck by late Saturday, the sources said.

"We estimate the yacht will arrive in the area where the accident was reported at 23:00 hours continental (Chilean) time (0300 GMT)," a spokesman in the office of Easter Island's maritime governer told Reuters.

The storm that wrecked the 99 foot (30 meter)-long Mata Rangi ship hit on Thursday night, and the expedition captain, Spanish sailor Kitin Munoz, managed to contact the Chilean navy on Friday afternoon by satellite phone.
According to his report, the entire 11-member crew and two stowaways had survived by using lifeboats,

The Mata Rangi (Eyes of Paradise) expedition has had a run of bad luck. Spain's Prince Felipe came for the launch in late April but it was delayed until May 6, without the prince present, because of bad weather and last-minute technical hitches.
Shortly after hitting the water, two stowaways with criminal records were found hiding among the supplies, and could not be returned because the ship was too far from Easter Island.
Last week another storm nearly forced the expedition to turn back, but it continued even after it lost a copper bar used for its antennae.
Chilean experts have questioned the project's historical veracity, saying the ship is much larger than any vessel known to have been used by ancient Polynesians.
